key_insight: Modern MoE designs can unintentionally undermine routing exploration: adding shared experts may reduce how much the router learns to diversify expert usage. The paper argues that routing and expert-sharing should be co-designed, especially when using fine-grained expert segmentation.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the exploration dilemma in modern mixture-of-experts models, where shared experts and finer expert segmentation can make routing less exploratory and harder to optimize effectively.
method: Analyzes the interaction between fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts in modern MoE routing.
Identifies how shared experts can reduce routing exploration and create a training imbalance.
Proposes a rethinking of routing design to preserve exploration while retaining the benefits of shared experts.
impact: For AI practitioners, this helps build MoE systems that scale better without sacrificing expert diversity or training effectiveness. It can improve model efficiency, routing stability, and overall performance in large-scale sparse architectures.
visual_elements: A split-panel diagram showing 'fine-grained experts' vs. 'shared experts' and their effect on routing behavior
A flowchart illustrating the exploration dilemma in the router during training
A heatmap of expert selection frequency before and after improved routing
An icon-based comparison of sparse activation patterns and shared expert activation
paper_title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Bingcong Li, Hao Ma, Michael Muehlebach, Niao He, Yi Ma
